answer.text: Rate of change of delta as spot changes

explanation.text: The Logic: Gamma is the rate of change of an option's delta with respect to a change in the price of the underlying (the second derivative of option price w.r.t. spot). Theta is time decay; the strike of a listed contract does not "change"; rho relates to interest rates. Note: Option Greeks (delta, gamma, theta, vega, rho) are not covered in the PMS Distributors (XXI-A) derivatives chapter, which is limited to derivative definitions, forwards/futures/options/swaps purposes, settlement, margins, and PMS-derivative permissions. Treat this as general option-pricing theory rather than XXI-A-syllabus content; deeper Greeks coverage is in NISM Series VIII.
